anchors.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: MNE-BIDS is a software tool for organizing electrophysiological data into BIDS, used to format this dataset; it does not describe the EEG-Asymmetries dataset itself.

anchors.paper_title: EEG-BIDS, an extension to the brain imaging data structure for electroencephalography
anchors.reason: EEG-BIDS is a data-organization standard/extension the dataset follows, not a paper describing this EEG asymmetries dataset.

metadata.methods_description: Participants completed a resting-state recording (~8 minutes, alternating open/closed eyes in 63s blocks) followed by four tasks (words, faces, emotions, houses) presented in randomized order. Each task included a practice block and two response blocks (right-hand and left-hand responses), with stimuli presented for 1 second followed by a fixation cross (500-700ms). Each task consisted of 160 stimulus presentations total, with participants responding via spacebar press only to specific target stimuli (animal names, female faces, houses with pitched roofs).
